finite_inference.explanation: For the two named dictionary spellings only, the -icis genitive and feminine mute-stem paradigm yield Genitrice and Genetrice, with the same -e ablative ending. This statement is an explicitly reviewed grammatical inference, not a transcription of an ablative printed in the lexicon and not permission to generate any other form.

required_contextual_parse: In each separately pinned complete prayer, intercedente beata Virgine Dei Genitrice/Genetrice Maria is an ablative absolute. Genitrice/Genetrice is feminine ablative singular appositional to Virgine Maria, the same third-person intercessor; Dei is dependent genitive; Domine is the vocative addressee. No person, referent, grammatical case, number, gender or sense is changed.
qualifications: The Orthographical Index prefers genetrix and acknowledges differences among manuscript/edition spellings and authorities; no equal-preference claim.
The main entry characterizes usage as poetical and in post-Augustan prose; retain this source register judgment.
Lewis and Short title is undated and damaged; registered1879 edition and catalogue1899 impression remain distinct.
Allen and Greenough1903 US publication remains qualified by actual1888/1903 copyright notices and1903 dated preface; pencil dates and printer code are not independent dating.
required_per_prayer: Use only the exact target identity, original source/target/English strings, complete current Latin proof dictionary and raw full-row/declaration hashes enumerated here.
Token12 zero-based (13 one-based) must literally read Genitrice in source and Genetrice in target. Full context must support the stated apposition.
All other spelling pairs, punctuation and conclusion differences need their separate existing authorizations; this method changes none of them.
Retain every original source/target/English byte, predecessor refusal and dated source review; this comparison is not a new translation or a normalized donor lookup.
excluded: All other targets and token positions.
All unlisted forms or cases, generic stem folding, e/i conversion and generated paradigms.
Names, compounds, printer-error repair, sanctus/beatus, different persons/referents, homographs and semantic substitutions.
Cross-owner donor reuse or automatic fanout.
Any conclusion-family, short-cue or English-word expansion.
English January1 admission: its independent conclusion/materialization hold remains separate.
Chantal Postcommunion: remains held, outside this method.
root_disposition: Source-only independent primary-image review and the explicit feminine third-declension inference support only the two exact contexts. Require installation of the ten reviewed source postimages and complete per-prayer current joins. January1 English remains held on its separate conclusion issue. This accepts no English prayer, other form, donor reuse, or conclusion expansion.

full_current_target_proof.provenance_evidence: The project-owned projection passage reproduces the retained calendar body hash exactly. Its artifact manifest records the bounded public-domain 1862 Pustet antecedent, the separate 1962 target, and every editorial transformation; neither witness is represented as owning the projected bytes. The 1962 reading was established on that edition's page images rather than its text layer, cross-read against the Benziger conformed printing. Differences from the antecedent: token 0: 1962 prints "Haec"; 1922 Tours Mame reads "Zc" (edit distance 2); token 12: 1962 prints "Genetrice"; 1922 Tours Mame reads "Genitrice" (edit distance 1); token 20: 1962 prints "eundem"; 1922 Tours Mame reads "eumdem" (edit distance 1, conclusion); 1922 Mame prints Genitrice where the 1962 prints Genetrice; 1922 Mame sets the conclusion in parentheses. Corroboration: 1862 Pustet Ratisbon text-layer lines 16671-16684: 15 of 22 tokens identical after normalisation (n-gram similarity 0.68); 1604 Vatican typical: swept end to end, no matching text (best window n-gram similarity 0.44, which is noise).
